item.title: Capricor vs Nippon Shinyaku Lawsuit
item.description:
• Summary: Capricor Therapeutics has filed a breach of contract lawsuit against its U.S. partner Nippon Shinyaku over plans for a Duchenne muscular dystrophy drug. Capricor accuses Nippon of slow-walking commercialization preparations and pricing flaws. The lawsuit highlights tensions in the partnership for the Duchenne therapy, likely CAP-1002.
  • MoAs: CAP-1002 is an allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cell therapy that promotes tissue regeneration and immunomodulation.
  • Sources: STAT News, Fierce Pharma, Endpoints News

item.title: Daiichi Sankyo ADC Manufacturing Loss
item.description:
• Summary: Daiichi Sankyo reported an extraordinary loss of nearly $1 billion, with a $610 million profit hit linked to losses in its antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) manufacturing operations. The losses are associated with manufacturing issues for its ADC portfolio, which includes blockbuster drugs like Enhertu.
  • MoAs: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) combine a monoclonal antibody targeting specific antigens (e.g., HER2) with a cytotoxic payload (e.g., topoisomerase I inhibitor) for targeted cancer therapy.
  • Sources: Endpoints News, Fierce Pharma

item.title: Odyssey IPO
item.description:
• Summary: Odyssey Therapeutics raised over $300 million in its Nasdaq IPO to fund its pipeline of autoimmune and inflammatory disease therapies. The company, led by Gary Glick, plans to advance its precision immunology programs.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech, Endpoints News, BioPharma Dive

item.title: Roche Acquires PathAI
item.description:
• Summary: Roche has agreed to acquire PathAI, a startup in AI-powered pathology, for $750 million upfront. The deal aims to enhance Roche's diagnostics capabilities and integrate AI into pathology workflows.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: STAT News

item.title: Lilly Manufacturing Investment
item.description:
• Summary: Lilly announced a $4.5 billion investment in its Indiana manufacturing operations and opened the doors of its first genetic medicine manufacturing site. This expansion reflects Lilly's commitment to increasing production capacity for its growing pipeline, including gene therapies and other advanced modalities.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: Ascendis Retreats to Rare Endocrinology
item.description:
• Summary: Ascendis Pharma is pivoting away from oncology, retreating to its core strength in rare endocrinology after its cancer programs faltered. The company plans to focus on its TransCon technology platform for endocrine disorders, signaling a strategic shift in its pipeline priorities.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: Angelini to Buy Catalyst Pharmaceuticals
item.description:
• Summary: Angelini Pharma has agreed to acquire Catalyst Pharmaceuticals, a company known for its rare disease drug Firdapse (amifampridine) for Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS). The acquisition expands Angelini's portfolio in neurology and rare diseases.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Pharmaceutical Technology

item.title: Lilly Gilead Deal Leadership
item.description:
• Summary: Eli Lilly and Gilead Sciences lead the pharmaceutical industry in dealmaking activity, according to a report on mergers, acquisitions, and licensing. The article highlights their strategic priorities, including oncology and immunology, and how these transactions are reshaping their pipelines and market positions.
